pointers.sentence: An accepted request goes on to its view; a refused one gets the failure view's response in its place (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).

`CsrfViewMiddleware._accept` marks an accepted request with the attribute `"csrf_processing_done"`, and `process_view` returns at once for a request so marked, which is what lets the middleware and the `csrf_protect` decorator share one request ([A middleware as a decorator](../views/middleware-decorators.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._accept`).

Last, the test client's flag: its handler sets `"_dont_enforce_csrf_checks"` on every request, true unless the client was made with `enforce_csrf_checks=True` ([The test client: `Client` and `ClientHandler`](../testing/client.md)) (`django/test/client.py:ClientHandler.__call__`).

A request with an `"Origin"` header is refused unless `CsrfViewMiddleware._origin_verified` accepts it, in one of three ways tried in order (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._origin_verified`).

Or it may have the scheme of a trusted origin written with a `"*"`, and a host that matches that origin's host, star taken off, by `is_same_domain`, where a pattern that begins with a dot matches the domain and every subdomain (`django/utils/http.py:is_same_domain`).
The setting is read into three cached properties, once for each instance of the middleware (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.allowed_origin_subdomains`).

Otherwise the host must match the cookie's domain, `CSRF_COOKIE_DOMAIN` or, with `CSRF_USE_SESSIONS`, `SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, with the request's port added unless it is 443 or 80; or, when that domain is `None`, as by default, `get_host`, port and all, a `DisallowedHost` being refused (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._check_referer`).
No secret is refused too: insisting on a cookie for a `"POST"`, the comment says, avoids all CSRF attacks, login CSRF among them (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._check_token`).

`_does_token_match` unmasks a token of 64, takes one of 32 as the secret itself, as a script that read the cookie sends it, and compares it with the secret by `constant_time_compare` ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](keys.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:_does_token_match`).

It imports the view `CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` names by `get_callable`, calls it with the request and the reason, and logs the response by `log_response` to `"django.security.csrf"`, as `"Forbidden (%s): %s"` with the reason and the path (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._reject`).

`log_response` logs a 4xx as a warning and marks the response as logged, so the handler, which logs every response of 400 or more to `"django.request"`, does not log it again (`django/utils/log.py:log_response`).

`csrf_failure` builds its page's context: a translated title and sentence; the reason; `"no_referer"` and `"no_cookie"`, true when the reason is `REASON_NO_REFERER` or `REASON_NO_CSRF_COOKIE`, each with paragraphs for the user; `settings.DEBUG`, with the documentation's version for its links and a line for when it is off; and the nonce, merged in from the `csp` context processor (`django/views/csrf.py:csrf_failure`).

When no engine has it, `csrf_failure` renders the built-in `"csrf_403.html"` with an `Engine` of its own and the context, so the page does not depend on `TEMPLATES` (`django/views/csrf.py:csrf_failure`).

The built-in page shows the paragraphs for a missing `"Referer"` or cookie when the reason is one of those, and, with `settings.DEBUG` true, the reason and a list of what to check (`django/views/templates/csrf_403.html`).

The check is synchronous for another reason: `process_view` is a synchronous method, which the handler adapts to its own mode separately from the layer ([Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).
